Ethereal

/ih-THEER-ee-uhl/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ethereal means extremely delicate, light, and graceful in a way that seems too perfect or otherworldly for ordinary life

The soprano's ethereal high notes seemed to float above the orchestra rather than come from an actual human voice.

Worked Example

Photographs of the valley at dawn show mist curling low over the fields while the first sunlight turns the fog gold, giving the whole scene an ethereal quality, as if the landscape belonged to a dream rather than to any real place.

Nothing in the photograph is literally magical, but the delicate mist and soft golden light make the scene feel impossibly light and otherworldly — exactly the quality "ethereal" names.

How Ethereal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

otherworldly

otherworldly: stresses that something feels like it doesn't belong to ordinary reality

delicate

delicate: focuses on fragile lightness rather than an otherworldly feeling

airy

airy: a lighter, more everyday word for the same weightless quality

Antonyms

earthy

earthy: grounded, solid, and rooted in ordinary physical life

substantial

substantial: solid and weighty, the opposite of delicate lightness

How Strong Is It? — light → airy → ethereal

light vs. ethereal

light vs. ethereal: Something light simply doesn't feel heavy — a light scarf, for instance.

airy vs. ethereal

airy vs. ethereal: Something airy feels open and weightless, like a room full of sunlight and empty space.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ether-

Root — ether-: the upper, purest air; the heavens (Greek aither)

Suffix — -eal

Suffix — -eal: relating to, characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: "Ethereal" literally means "relating to the upper air" — the ancient Greeks imagined aither as the purest substance filling the heavens, far above the ordinary air we breathe, which is why "ethereal" still describes anything that feels too delicate and pure for the everyday world.

Use the root in a new word: ether

Use the root in a new word: ether: Chemists once used ether as an anesthetic, and old poets used the same word to describe the invisible substance they believed filled outer space.

Root Check

Word Choice

literary, poetic

Ethereal is a literary, somewhat elevated word. It's reserved for things whose lightness or delicacy feels almost magical — music, light, fabric, or atmosphere — and would sound out of place describing something ordinary or heavy.
